comments.author: @davemarcelo_
comments.text:
I know this comment is about five years late, but the talking points stemming from only an economic lens leaves a gap in explaining the Global North/South divide, especially with the absence of a critical lens on a geopolitical standpoint. Without the discussion of human development, the neocolonialism lens, the critical discussion about capitalism (and the slow approach toward late-stage capitalism), corruption in the Global South, and the ecological implication of the Industrial Revolution (and the continuous refusal of the Global North to act on climate change), the link between economic growth and geography will always seem to be a sterile, theoretical discussion. 

Then again, it is understood that it takes more than 10 minutes to discuss these.
